1.explanation:
• Toggle/README.md: Describes the component’s purpose, API and any accessibility notes; a good starting point to understand intended ARIA behavior.
• Toggle/index.js: The entry point that wires up the Toggle component—helpful to see how props (like aria-hidden) are passed down.
• Toggle/Toggle.js: The core implementation where the <input> and <span> text elements are rendered and where aria-hidden="true" is applied; you’ll need to adjust this markup to restore label announcements.
• Toggle/Toggle.scss: Contains the class names (e.g. .bx–toggle__text-left, .bx–toggle__text-right) referenced in the screenshot—useful to verify no CSS is inadvertently hiding elements.
• Toggle/Toggle.stories.js: Shows how the Toggle is used in Storybook, reproducing the interactive scenario and allowing quick iteration on ARIA fixes.
1.bug_scenario: The issue occurs in the default Toggle component when VoiceOver is used on macOS Mojave. After tabbing into the toggle and hitting Enter or Space, VoiceOver does not announce the “On”/“Off” labels. In the DOM you can see two <span> elements for the left and right label with aria-hidden="true", which is hiding those state labels from assistive technology. The screenshot shows the rendered Toggle with its inner structure: an <input type="checkbox"> wrapped by a <label> that contains three spans (left text, appearance, right text) with both text spans marked aria-hidden.
